sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (December 1997), 238 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 1 'Special Relativity' printed pp. 4-10 and 25-31 (PDF pp. 11-17 and 32-38): the flat metric eta = diag(-1,1,1,1), causal classification, worldlines, proper time and four-velocity; Ch. 2 printed pp. 31 and 48-54 (PDF pp. 37 and 55-61): the torus by identification of opposite sides, manifolds, metric components in a chart; Ch. 3 printed pp. 70-71 (PDF pp. 77-78): the geodesic equation; Ch. 4 printed pp. 105-127 (PDF pp. 112-134): weak fields, the Newtonian limit, linearized equations, field equations and Misner space; Ch. 5 printed pp. 140-142 (PDF pp. 147-149): Killing vectors; Ch. 6 printed pp. 142-151 (PDF pp. 149-158): linearized field equations and the retarded Green function.

contents.name: Ch. 1 pp. 6-10: the Lorentz metric eta and the classification of tangent vectors
contents.support: The metric components diag(-1,1,1,1) in the inertial chart, the causal classification and the future cone are the definition's clauses (a)-(c); the source's time-orientation convention is the model's N = partial_0.

contents.name: Ch. 1 (1.97)-(1.99) pp. 25-27: worldlines, proper time and four-velocity
contents.support: Clause (d) of the lemma proves that the affine parametrization of a future timelike geodesic with eta(v,v) = -1 is proper time with dgamma/dtau of unit norm; the source's formulas are the same identities for straight lines.

contents.name: Ch. 1 pp. 26-27: the low-velocity expansions E = m + (1/2)mv^2 and p = mv
contents.support: The lemma makes the expansions uniform with explicit Lagrange remainders; the source's leading terms are the first-order parts.

contents.name: Ch. 2 p. 31: the n-torus by identifying opposite sides of a cube
contents.support: The counterexample performs the same identification construction for the flat model, with the translation group and the exact quotient metric proved by the quotient lemma.

contents.name: Ch. 2 pp. 48-51: metric components in a chart and the transformation law
contents.support: The constant components in the identity chart are the definition's clause (a); the transformation law is carried by the library's covariant-tensor machinery.

contents.name: Ch. 3 (3.47) pp. 70-71: the geodesic equation and straight lines as the geodesics of flat space
contents.support: Clauses (a) and (d) prove the vanishing connection and the if-and-only-if affine-line description, with the maximal domain and the speed computed.

contents.name: Ch. 4 pp. 105-112: the weak-field and slow-motion conditions g_00 = -(1+2Phi), g_ij = (1-2Phi) delta_ij and the Newtonian limit
contents.support: The data's component form, the potential Phi = epsilon c^2 phi and the derivative bounds restate the source's ansatz with explicit uniformity hypotheses; the Poisson equation is derived in the hierarchy theorem.

contents.name: Ch. 4 pp. 106-110 (PDF pp. 113-117): the linearized Ricci and Einstein tensors, the trace-reversed perturbation and harmonic gauge
contents.support: Clauses (a)-(d) compute the first-order coefficients in closed form and prove the trace-reversal, gauge-transformation and harmonic-gauge identities.

contents.name: Ch. 4 pp. 124-127 (PDF pp. 131-134): Misner space and the warning that identifications can produce closed timelike curves
contents.reason: Misner space identifies points along a boosted direction so its light cones tilt in time; the page's quotient counterexample is the different rolled-up flat model with constant metric components, and the tilted model belongs to the causal-structure track.

contents.name: Ch. 4 pp. 109-112: the motion of test particles in the weak field, d^2x/dt^2 = -grad Phi
contents.support: The lemma proves the coordinate-time reparametrization identity and the uniform error |x'' + grad Phi| <= C_3 c^2 epsilon^2/L, of which the source's equation is the leading term.

contents.name: Ch. 5 pp. 140-142: Killing vectors and conserved quantities along geodesics
contents.support: Clause (c) proves that the coordinate fields are Killing fields of the flat metric via the flow definition; the conserved-quantity reading belongs to the framework's postulates.

contents.name: Ch. 6 (6.1)-(6.9) pp. 142-151: the linearized field equations, retarded Green function and range of validity
contents.support: The theorem solves the gauge wave equation Box xi_b = partial^a hbar_ab with zero data on all of R^4 by spherical means and Duhamel's formula, a self-contained treatment of the source's Green-function discussion; the quadratic-range warning is carried by the remainder clause of the linearization theorem.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), 125 PDF pages
sources.locator: Sections 1.1, 2.1, 3.3-3.4, 4.1-4.2, 7.1-7.2: four-momentum and low-velocity readings; charts, metric components and the flat metric as trivial solution; the geodesic equation, proper time and normal coordinates; the Newtonian limit and weak fields; perturbations, trace reversal and de Donder gauge.

contents.name: Section 1.1 pp. 5-8: four-momentum, rest mass and low-velocity energy and momentum
contents.support: The lemma states the observer-relative identities with uniform remainder bounds; the source's expansions are the leading terms.

contents.name: Section 2.1 pp. 25-27: charts, metric components, canonical form of a Lorentzian form and the flat metric in Cartesian coordinates
contents.support: The definition fixes the metric components diag(-1,1,1,1) in the inertial chart and the Lorentzian signature; the vanishing connection is proved separately on this page.

contents.name: Section 3.3 pp. 37-39: the geodesic equation and proper time as an affine parameter in flat spacetime
contents.support: Clause (d) proves the affine-line description and the proper-time parametrization of future timelike geodesics.

contents.name: Section 3.4 pp. 38-40: normal coordinates and the curvature obstruction to making metric derivatives vanish
contents.support: The remark records the pointwise-versus-curvature distinction; the exponential-chart theorem proves the local isometry direction.

contents.name: Section 4.1 pp. 41-43: the flat metric on R^4 as the trivial solution of the field equations
contents.support: Clause (a) of the physics theorem verifies the flat model against the adopted field law with Lambda = 0 and T = 0.

contents.name: Section 4.2 p. 42: weak fields, slow motion and the Poisson equation
contents.support: The stationary weak-field data and the potential fix the source's weak-field regime with explicit derivative bounds; the Poisson reduction is the hierarchy theorem.

contents.name: Sections 7.1-7.2 pp. 86-92: perturbations of the metric, the trace-reversed perturbation and the de Donder gauge condition, with the neglected second-order terms
contents.support: Clauses (c)-(f) give the first-order coefficients, the gauge identities, the harmonic-gauge reduction and the quadratic remainder bound.

contents.name: The Newtonian module: the controlled weak-field and slow-motion expansion of the geodesic equation
contents.support: The theorem compares the scaled geodesic trajectory with the Newtonian system on a fixed scaled interval with an explicit Gronwall error, making the source's expansion uniform.

sources.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), 289 PDF pages
sources.locator: Sections 1.2 pp. 12-19 (metric, causal classification, energy-momentum and its nonrelativistic limit); 3.3.1-3.3.2 pp. 119-121 (the geodesic equation and normal coordinates); 5.1-5.1.2 pp. 205-210 (the weak-field ansatz, gauge freedom, the Newtonian limit and the Poisson equation); 6.3.2 pp. 272-273 (closed timelike curves from a periodic coordinate direction).

contents.name: Section 1.2.1 pp. 12-16: the metric eta on R^4 with x^mu = (ct,x,y,z) and the causal classification of tangent vectors
contents.support: The inertial chart, the metric components and the causal/future classification are the definition's content.

contents.name: Section 1.2 pp. 15-19: the relativistic energy-momentum relation and its nonrelativistic limit
contents.support: The lemma proves the exact identities and the uniform low-velocity bounds whose leading terms are the source's expansions.

contents.name: Section 3.3.1 pp. 119-121: the geodesic equation and the statement that constant-velocity straight lines are the geodesics of the flat metric
contents.support: Clause (d) proves the if-and-only-if affine-line description together with maximality and the velocity reading.

contents.name: Section 3.3.2 pp. 119-121: normal coordinates and the obstruction to making second derivatives of the metric vanish
contents.support: The remark states the three-level separation (pointwise flatness, vanishing curvature, global geometry); the exponential-chart theorem proves the local isometry.

contents.name: Sections 5.1-5.1.1 pp. 205-208: the stationary weak-field ansatz g = eta + h with h_00 = -2Phi, h_ij = -2Phi delta_ij, gauge freedom and the force law
contents.support: The theorem derives the component hierarchy of the Einstein tensor and the stress-energy hierarchy with uniform error terms, of which the source's leading expressions are the first-order parts.

contents.name: Section 5.1.2 pp. 208-210: the Newtonian limit, the Poisson equation and the de Donder gauge condition
contents.support: The Poisson reduction is the hierarchy theorem's clause (c) and the trajectory correspondence is proved in the scaled comparison theorem; the constant-density case is worked on the companion page.

contents.name: Section 5.1.1 p. 210: the warning that the isotropic spatial metric -2Phi delta_ij must be compared with the areal-radius Schwarzschild form through the isotropic coordinate transformation
contents.reason: The comparison requires the isotropic-to-areal coordinate transformation of the spherically symmetric vacuum model, which is built on the later page gr-spherical-vacuum-model; this page keeps the weak-field family in a fixed inertial chart and states no radial-coordinate identification.

contents.name: Section 6.3.2 pp. 272-273: a periodic coordinate direction of negative norm produces a closed timelike curve
contents.support: The counterexample's closed future timelike curve arises exactly this way, from the periodic time coordinate of the rolled-up flat model; the source's Kerr-interior example is a different metric.

sources.title: V. Ivrii, Partial Differential Equations (University of Toronto, 2018)
sources.locator: Section 2.5.2: the spherical-mean construction for the wave equation and the Duhamel formula, used as the comparison treatment for the local proof of the all-space zero-data solution.

contents.name: Section 2.5.2: spherical means and the Duhamel formula for the wave equation
contents.support: The theorem proves the spherical-mean reduction, the zero-data solution and the Duhamel integral self-containedly, with explicit smoothness and differentiation-under-the-integral hypotheses; the source is a comparison treatment of the same technique.

sources.title: G. B. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorems 2.27 and 2.49
sources.locator: Chapter 2: Theorem 2.27 (differentiation under the integral sign) and Theorem 2.49 (polar coordinates), the classical statements of the measure-theoretic inputs cited for the spherical-mean computation.

contents.name: Theorems 2.27 and 2.49: differentiation under the integral sign and polar coordinates
contents.support: The theorem's proof cites the library's own measure-theoretic suppliers for both inputs and carries the Axiom of Countable Choice explicitly; the source is the classical comparison reference.

sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (December 1997), 238 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 4 printed pp. 105-151 (PDF pp. 112-158): weak fields, the Newtonian limit, linearized curvature and the field equations, the source of the explicit perturbation and of the quadratic-remainder warning.

contents.name: Ch. 4 pp. 106-112: the linearized Ricci tensor for a diagonal perturbation and its use in the Newtonian limit
contents.support: The example inserts the explicit quadratic potential into the first-order formulas and checks the resulting coefficients by two independent routes.

contents.name: Ch. 4 pp. 109-112: test-particle motion in the weak-field potential
contents.support: The comparison system's harmonic solution and its compact convex range are verified explicitly for the quadratic potential.

contents.name: Ch. 4 pp. 106-110: the quadratic terms omitted in the linearized expansion
contents.support: The counterexample computes the exact Ricci component of a first-order vacuum family and shows the quadratic failure explicitly.

sources.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), 289 PDF pages
sources.locator: Sections 1.2 pp. 15-19 (low-speed expansions); 3.3.1 pp. 119-121 (straight-line geodesics of flat space); 5.1-5.1.2 pp. 205-210 (weak-field ansatz, force law, Poisson equation); 6.3.2 pp. 272-273 (periodic direction and closed timelike curves).

contents.name: Section 1.2 pp. 15-19: low-speed energy and momentum expansions
contents.support: The example evaluates the exact identities and the uniform bounds at relative speed c/2 with rational/algebraic comparisons.

contents.name: Section 3.3.1 pp. 119-121: straight constant-velocity geodesics of the flat metric
contents.support: The example evaluates the worldline, coordinate velocity and clock identity at an explicit future timelike vector.

contents.name: Sections 5.1-5.1.2 pp. 205-210: the weak-field ansatz and the Poisson equation with constant density
contents.support: The example verifies the data hypotheses with explicit constants and solves the Poisson equation exactly with the constant density for the quadratic potential.

contents.name: Section 6.3.2 pp. 272-273: a periodic negative-norm direction as a closed timelike curve
contents.support: The counterexample's closed future timelike curve and the failure of global Minkowski geometry are proved for the rolled-up flat model.
